c1006.summary: Tyagaraja's salutation to all the great souls — the devotees, sages and musicians who have realised God through love, music and knowledge.
m: There are so many great souls — my salutations to every one of them.
Those who behold the beauty of the moon-hued Lord in the lotus of their heart
and experience supreme bliss —
the blessed foremost ones who delight in Sama chanting, lovely as Manmatha —
those who let the mind roam freely in the forest of the heart and praise His form well —
those who readily offer the lotus of their heart at His feet —
those who, along the true path to the Supreme who purifies the fallen,
sing, converse, and know the ragas with their svara and laya —
devotees who wear Hari's virtues like jewelled garlands, and with wisdom,
affection and compassion protect the whole world with a nectar-like gaze —
those who always gaze on the graceful Lord of charming gait,
thrilled in body, immersed in an ocean of bliss, renowned for that joy —
the great devotees and sages, the moon and the sun, Sanaka and Sanandana,
the guardians of the directions, gods, Kimpurushas, Prahlada son of Hiranyakashipu, Narada and Tumburu,
Hanuman son of the Wind, Shiva who wears the crescent moon, Shuka, Brahma and the best of Brahmins,
the supremely pure, the great, the eternal, ever enjoying bliss — and besides them,
those who know your form, your name and glory, your valour, courage and serene mind,
the truth of your word, O Raghuvara, and how devotion to you overturns false doctrines —
and who, knowing your heart, joyfully sing kirtanas of your virtues —
those who know the secrets of the Bhagavata, Ramayana, Gita, Vedas, Shastras and Puranas, and the teachings of Shiva and others,
and the inner feelings of the thirty-three crore gods, and the joy of bhava, raga and laya,
who live long in endless bliss and are dear to Tyagaraja —
those who utter the Name as love wells up, true servants of Rama praised by Tyagaraja.

c1011.summary: A Sanskrit garland of epithets for Rama, recounting his qualities and deeds; the first of Tyagaraja's Pancharatna kritis.
m: O source of the world's joy, victory to you, beloved lord of Janaki's life!
Born in the noble Solar race, king of kings, abode of virtues, served by the gods, ever the giver of good — (you who) all
a moon to the lily-like hosts of gods and stars, perfect one; a mountain and wish-tree to the gods,
the cow of plenty; dweller on the milk ocean; with the most handsome face; whose speech is nectar,
Govinda, ever joyful, consort of Lakshmi, beyond age, giver of good fortune, the one and the many,
nourisher of Brahma born of the lotus; the wind that scatters the clouds of the gods' enemies,
rider of Garuda; dwelling in the hearts of true poets; whose feet are worshipped by countless monkey chiefs,
lustrous as a sapphire, with sun and moon for eyes, immeasurable,
father of Brahma, lord of all, pure, reclining on the serpent king, praised by Shiva,
whose foot freed the sage's wife from her curse; protector of the sacrifice; eager to receive the sacred mantra,
supremely serene, lord of Janaki, giver of boons to Brahma, (giver of) all
cause of creation, preservation and dissolution, granter of every wish, of incomparable form,
praised by Indra; who humbled the ocean's pride; radiant with love; the essence of the epic,
a moon to the ocean of good men's minds; rider of the Pushpaka chariot; enemy of the gods' foes; whose lotus hands
are caressed (by Lakshmi); refuge of the virtuous; humbler of the gods' pride; eternal one, praised
the parrot in the cage of Om; whose forms are Shiva, Brahma and Vishnu; slayer of Ravana,
dear to Shiva; compassionate; protector of those who surrender; delight of the good; changeless; essence of the Vedas,
bearer of a quiver of arrows; destroyer of the demons' pride; protector of Brahmins and gods,
whose deeds are sung by Valmiki; praised by Tyagaraja,
the ancient Person, son of a king, devoted to those who seek refuge, slayer of Viradha and Ravana,
sinless one who captivated Parashara's heart, praised by Tyagaraja,
of countless virtues, clad in gold, who pierced the sala trees, with feet radiant as the dawn, of boundless
wondrous greatness, dwelling in the hearts of good poets, worshipped by gods and sages with sacred water,
beloved of Lakshmi, a Narasimha to the elephant of sin, praised by Tyagaraja.

c1004.summary: A long confession: Tyagaraja lists the faults of a life lost to wealth, flattery and pleasure, and asks who but Rama could save such a person.
m: Which lord will save a wayward one like me? How many (are my faults)!
Drawn by wicked pleasures, sunk in them every moment —
O sun to the lotus heart of Lakshmi, beyond the reach of word and mind!
Forgetting that you dwell in all beings,
from childhood devoid of the nectar of bhajan, a mere quibbler,
who wandered flattering others to melt their hearts, for their wealth, to fill my belly,
spending all my days thinking worldly comfort is life itself,
advising ignorant actors, rogues, mean men and women to win them over, and rejoicing in it,
ignorant of svara and laya, of crooked nature, counting myself equal to true devotees,
trusting the pleasures of the eye — women, home, children, servants and endless wealth — O God of gods,
I trusted them wholly and forgot the worship of your lotus feet,
never remembering your lovely lotus face in my heart, blinded by arrogance,
seeking out wicked people and suffering, unable to shake off evil desires,
always erring, fickle of mind,
not realising human birth is rare, never attaining supreme bliss, a slave to pride, jealousy,
desire, greed and delusion, deceived — though born in a noble family,
doing lowly deeds, chasing worthless creeds and going astray,
I wandered some days for women, some for property, some for sons, some for heaps of money — O friend of Tyagaraja, (who will save) such a one?

c1033.summary: Tyagaraja playfully complains that Krishna/Rama has had his way: the Lord taught the right path, accepted his worship, yet still did not come near.
m: He has had his way, O mind!
Making false the words of the good path he himself taught, he held firm to his own resolve.
Speaking words to suit the moment,
as when he delighted Devaki and Vasudeva,
Lord Ranganatha, father of the holy Ganga, master of the tradition of music,
who, without fulfilling the gopis' heart's desire, made sport of them,
the Supreme who ever enchants women and makes them bow — and more,
Hari, who smiled as Yashoda kissed him lovingly as her son,
who loves his devotees, an ocean of virtues, who removes the troubles of birth and of Kali —
while I held him in my lotus heart, thinking so,
(I prayed) 'Hari! Ramachandra, lord of the Raghus, of gentle speech, reclining on Shesha,
who sees others' wives as sisters, praised by Brahma and the king of kings, flawless and pure,
lotus-eyed one' — even as I pleaded so, he did not protect me.
Lord of Venkata, radiant, highest of all, dwelling in the minds of the good,
wearing golden robes, a shining crown and earrings — Hari! — so
I praised him; Ramachandra, sung by Tyagaraja, best of men,
told me 'this is how true devotees live', and graciously accepted my worship;
he told me 'do not be angry', 'do not keep company with those averse to God',
'bear sorrow when it comes'; yet he, the giver of calm and self-control,
the Lord praised by Tyagaraja, did not come near me.

c1018.summary: The more one sees Rama, the more beautiful he is; Tyagaraja recalls Dhruva, Sita and Hanuman, and calls Shiva and the sages as witnesses to Rama's charm.
m: The more I see you, the more delightful you are, O you clad in gold —
day after day, (seeing) you in my mind with affection.
Your milk-white face, with boundless glory and grace —
Sita, her face radiant, glancing at you shyly from the corner of her eyes —
clad in garments bright as the rising sun, your neck adorned with jewelled garlands,
lotus-eyed, with fine cheeks and a shining crown — always, to my heart's content.
When Suruchi, his stepmother, spoke words that pierced like a spear,
did not Dhruva, unable to bear it, meditate on Hari and find bliss? So too
with a musk mark on your fair brow, who gave liberation to the noble Jatayu — when the son
of the Wind told of your greatness, did not Sita, learning it, love you and lose her heart?
Abode of bliss, wind to the clouds of the averse, dear one who roams the mind of Janaka,
wish-tree to the worthy, marked by virtues, pure bliss, rider of Garuda, holder of the discus,
supremely kind, ocean of compassion, dispeller of fear, O Lord of the Raghus —
one who, with overflowing love, clasps your lotus feet in his hands
is witness; Shiva of Kailasa, who delights in Rama's name, is witness;
and Narada, Parashara, Shuka, Shaunaka, Indra, Parvati and Sita
and the great ones are witness — O beautiful lord, dweller in the ocean of bliss, for those who seek refuge
ever full of love, praised by Tyagaraja, whose face outshines the moon, giver of boons — (the more I see) you.

c1329.summary: Tyagaraja pleads with Rama to come and protect him, unable to bear not seeing his smiling face, and wonders who is to blame for the delay.
m: Knowing my anguish at not seeing your smiling face, won't you come to protect me, O Sri Raghuvara?
O bearer of the mountain, aren't your attendants the ones who give you good counsel? Would they leave you like this?
Did Garuda, king of birds, not set out at once on hearing your command? Or did he say the earth is too far from the heavens?
O Supreme Being who rules the world, to whom else can I appeal? Don't show indifference — I cannot bear it. Take me as your own, O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c1003.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama for a soldier's post in his court; his armour, badge and sword are the thrill of devotion, the mark of a devotee, and Rama's name.
m: O Rama, grant me service in your court in the manner of a soldier —
(the service of one who) strikes down Manmatha, wielder of the sugarcane bow,
and pride and the other inner enemies, and fells them to the ground — that true service.
The thrill of devotion as my mighty armour,
the badge proclaiming me Rama's devotee,
and the fine sword that is Rama's name — these
shine on this Tyagaraja, O Lord.

c1024.summary: Why does Rama hide himself? Tyagaraja has realised that Rama is everything, and can think of no one else.
m: Why this veil, O Raghava?
Why hide, you whose form is all that moves and is still, highest of the high, whose eyes are the sun and moon?
Searching deep within, I have firmly realised that you are everything.
Seeing only you, I cannot think of others; protect me, O one praised by Tyagaraja.

c1478.summary: Tyagaraja's answer when called to the royal court: is wealth happiness, or service in Rama's presence?
m: Is wealth the greater happiness, or service in Rama's presence? Tell me truly, O mind.
Are curd, butter and milk tastier, or the nectar of meditating on and singing of Dasharatha's son?
Is bathing in the Ganga of self-control and calm happier, or bathing in the muddy well of base pleasures?
Is praise of men bound by attachment happier, or kirtanas on the Lord praised by Tyagaraja?

c2757.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama, who shines in everything from an ant to Brahma, why he hesitates to protect him.
m: O Rama, protect me — why do you hesitate, O Lord of the worlds?
You who shine lovingly in the ant and in Brahma, in Shiva and Keshava — who bear that very title, Lord of Sita,
I do not strut about seeking praise; I live without wrongdoing — protect me, Lord of Sita, praised by Tyagaraja.

c2303.summary: On the indescribable charm of Rama, and on those who wear the garb of devotees while chasing pleasures.
m: How charming, how beautiful you are! Who could describe it?
However great they may be, they fall into worry and longing over women,
and, slaves to the desire for pleasures, they put on the guise of true devotees.
Can a ladle know the taste of the milk it holds? (Such are they) — while the Lord praised by Tyagaraja is foremost.

c1044.summary: A meditation on the seven notes as deities who dwell in the body, the Vedas and the hearts of the wise.
m: Worship, O mind, the beautiful deities of the seven notes, who shine forth
in the navel, heart, throat, tongue, nose and other places,
in the Rig and Sama Vedas and the rest, in the heart of the sacred Gayatri,
in the minds of gods and Brahmins, and in Tyagaraja himself.

c1486.summary: Tyagaraja scolds his own mind for not listening to his advice to worship Rama instead of keeping bad company.
m: O mind, how am I to bear with you? Won't you heed my plea?
When I asked you to worship the jewel of the Solar race humbly
and spend your days so, why don't you listen, you worthless one?
In this Kali age, keeping company with people of restless and dull nature,
mingling and roaming with them — instead of wasting time,
I can cross (this ocean) easily: the hints that make this known —
Tyagaraja's words — why don't you listen, you worthless one?

c1036.summary: A Sanskrit hymn to Krishna as the master of music born of the Sama Veda, who delights in playing the flute.
m: O you of graceful elephant-like gait, sun to the lotus hearts of the good, beyond time, renowned one,
master of nectar-like music born of the Sama Veda, of noble character, abode of compassion — protect me.
You who embraced the seven notes born of the crown of the Vedas, the lamp on the mountain of nada,
born in the Yadava clan, delighting in playing the flute, enchanting one, worshipped by Tyagaraja.

c1116.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama to understand the secret in his heart: he has no one but Rama.
m: Know the secret in my heart, O protector of honour, emerald-hued one,
dear one of the Solar race — apart from you I have no one, O blissful heart.
Long ago you were a loving lord; why deny me that affection now? Is that greatness?
When will you take my hand in yours, O one praised by Tyagaraja?

c2293.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama why he won't grant him the wisdom of the great ones — knowledge of the Vedas, Vedanta and the science of music.
m: Why won't you give me wisdom like that of the elders? Where would it go, O Ramayya?
Like everyone else I overstepped again and again and babbled, and became a fruit beyond reach.
(Wisdom) to know the truth and meaning of the Vedas and Shastras, and Vedanta that sees no difference,
and to know the secrets of the science of nada — truly, O Lord praised by Tyagaraja.

c1517.summary: Devotion steeped in svara and raga is itself liberation; music without knowledge, or worship without a pure mind, is empty.
m: Devotion steeped in the nectar of svara and raga is heaven and liberation, O mind.
It is supreme bliss itself — what can the crane and the frog beside the lotus know of it, O mind?
Knowing the nada that rises from the Muladhara is joyful liberation;
knowing the resounding seven svaras and their home notes is liberation, O mind.
Becoming a knower after many births is liberation;
one who has knowledge of raga with natural devotion is liberated, O mind.
Is it joy to pound the drum without knowing the rhythms of tala?
Worship without a pure mind is a pig's way of life, O mind.
The secrets of the ocean of svaras that Shiva of the silver mountain told Parvati —
victorious Tyagaraja knows them; trust and learn them, O mind.

c2271.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama what he would lose by appearing before him, and protests against his indifference.
m: If you stood before me, what of yours would be lost?
Could I go beyond what is written on my forehead? Would I knowingly be deceived?
Look on me fairly; understand my needs; I cannot keep asking for boons.
O king of all gods, hear my plea, destroyer of sin, of handsome form, my
Lord, beloved of Videha's daughter — this is the time to protect me; I won't beg other gods.
Don't you know my mind, Raghava? What heroism is this, again and again, toward me?
If you show me this unheard-of indifference, Rama, would gods and demons praise you?
Why this callousness now, O Lord praised by your devotee Tyagaraja?

c1804.summary: Tyagaraja begs Rama for pure devotion, without which all learning is like adorning a corpse.
m: Grant me the alms of devotion, auspicious and pure —
devotion that is the root of liberation and all power, greater even than the Trimurtis, O Rama.
Like wrapping a golden turban and diamond ornaments on one who has no life — so it is for the learned (without devotion);
what use are Puranas, Agamas, Shastras, Vedas and japa without it? O Rama, praised by your devotee Tyagaraja.

c1475.summary: Tyagaraja asks Rama whether it is fair to look at him askance.
m: Is it fair to look at me askance, O best of the Raghus, for one like you?
Tell me, what bond do you have with your servants who call you lotus-eyed?
Did it not occur to you at all to protect my honour? What is that to you, O embodiment of virtue?
Protector of the lowly, who delights in the music of those who seek refuge, praised by Tyagaraja.
